name: get_addon_status
description: Check the connected Blender version, add-on version, and capabilities before starting a task. If up_to_date is false, follow update_command and after_install.

name: get_scene_info
description: Inspect the active scene, mode, selection, camera, units, and a page of objects sorted by name. Defaults to 20 objects; use next_offset with the same filters to continue until null. Filters combine with AND. Pages reflect live scene state: restart at offset 0 after adding, removing, or renaming objects. Use get_object_info for full transforms, bounds, and modifiers.

name_filter.description: Case-insensitive substring of the object name. Omit for all names.

object_type.description: Blender object type in uppercase, for example MESH, CURVE, EMPTY, CAMERA, or LIGHT.

selected_only.description: Only selected objects in the active view layer (default false).

name: get_object_info
description: Inspect an object by exact name: local transforms, world matrix and location, dimensions, parent, collections, modifiers, visibility, materials, and mesh counts/bounds. Local location and Euler rotation (radians) are relative to the parent; use matrix_world for the full world transform. Top-level mesh counts describe the base mesh; bounds and dimensions use cached object bounds. With evaluated=true, adds evaluated data for the current frame and viewport dependency graph: mesh counts after modifiers, instance sources with per-copy mesh counts, mesh_including_instances totals, and world bounds/dimensions including generated instances. Evaluated bounds enclose transformed local mesh bounds. Meshes, curves, surfaces, text, and metaballs contribute mesh geometry; other types have null mesh, and bounds/dimensions are null when there are no vertices. Requires the object in the active view layer dependency graph. May be expensive for dense geometry. Camera objects also include projection, lens in millimetres, field-of-view angles in radians, sensor size/fit, shift, clipping, active-camera state, and depth-of-field settings.

object_name.description: Exact object name returned by scene inspection or code execution.

evaluated.description: Include evaluated mesh counts, instance-source summaries, and bounds including instances (default false). Uses viewport modifier settings at the current frame.

name: set_camera
description: Change camera projection, lens (millimetres), orthographic scale, shift, or clipping, and optionally make it the active scene camera. With object_names, fit evaluated object bounds while preserving camera orientation; padding adds a margin and fitting overrides ortho_scale. Clipping planes are not adjusted automatically. Supports perspective and orthographic fitting; mute camera constraints before fitting. Changes shared camera data. Returns camera settings and world transform. Inspect exact camera and target names first.

object_name.description: Exact camera object name in the active scene.

lens.description: Focal length in millimetres; changes perspective camera zoom.

ortho_scale.description: Orthographic camera scale in scene units; smaller values zoom in.

clip_start.description: Near clipping distance; must be less than clip_end.

clip_end.description: Far clipping distance; must exceed clip_start.

object_names.description: Exact names of objects to frame, including evaluated instances.

make_active.description: Make this the scene camera (default false).

name: set_viewport
description: Inspect or change a 3D viewport. Omit settings to inspect its current state. Set view direction, projection, shading, overlays, gizmos, or zoom. Frame ALL visible objects, SELECTED visible objects, or exact object_names, including evaluated instances. Framing preserves selection and exits camera view; it cannot be combined with distance. Axis views default to orthographic and ISO to perspective. CAMERA uses the viewport camera and accepts camera_zoom for display zoom; use set_camera to change the actual camera lens or fit its composition. Requires a Blender window with a single-view 3D viewport.

viewport_index.description: 3D viewport index across windows, current window first (default 0). Quad view is unsupported.

frame.description: Objects to frame; cannot be combined with object_names.

object_names.description: Exact names of objects to frame, including evaluated instances.

distance.description: Absolute distance from the viewport pivot; unavailable in camera view.

camera_zoom.description: Blender camera-view display zoom from -30 to 600; 0 is the default. Does not change rendered composition.

name: get_viewport_screenshot
description: Capture a 3D viewport as an image with dimensions, capture method, and viewport settings. Requires a Blender window with a single-view 3D viewport. Use set_viewport to frame objects and choose shading. With camera_only=true, capture the active scene camera frame using viewport shading and render pixel aspect; supports PERSP and ORTHO cameras. This is a viewport preview; use render jobs for final camera renders. Camera capture leaves the displayed view unchanged and requires offscreen capture; normal viewport capture can fall back to a window grab.

max_size.description: Maximum pixel size of the largest image dimension.

viewport_index.description: 3D viewport index across windows, current window first (default 0). Quad view is unsupported.

camera_only.description: Capture only the active scene camera frame (default false).

name: execute_blender_code
description: Execute Python on Blender's main thread with bpy already available. Prefer bpy.data for edits; bpy.ops may require a specific mode, selection, or context override. Print concise results: expressions are not returned automatically. Python stdout/stderr are limited to 16,384 characters each. Errors include traceback and output; earlier changes are not rolled back. Optional checkpoint saves a .blend copy before execution; summarize_changes reports created, changed, and removed objects, including on failure. Either option adds an execution_id retrievable with get_execution_result. A timeout does not cancel execution: inspect before retrying. Without namespace, globals are fresh each call. A task-specific namespace preserves imports, variables, and helpers until reset, checkpoint restoration, or server restart. Namespaces separate globals only; Blender data and imported modules are shared.

code.description: Python statements to execute. Use print(...) to return values; empty code is allowed for namespace reset.

namespace.description: Unique task ID for persistent globals. Anyone using the same ID shares its globals.

reset_namespace.description: Clear this namespace before executing code; requires namespace when true. Use empty code to release stored variables when finished.

checkpoint.description: Save a checkpoint before running code (default false). Requires Object mode and a free checkpoint slot; if saving fails, code does not run. Returns checkpoint metadata on success or failure. Does not roll back automatically. External files and Python state are not saved.

summarize_changes.description: Compare objects before and after execution (default false). Requires Object mode initially; reports summary_error if the final state cannot be inspected. Covers writable object/data properties, relationships, modifier/constraint settings, material slots, and base mesh positions/topology. Excludes shader contents, animation, mesh attributes, scene settings, external files, and Python state. Full counts with at most 100 names per category; scans all objects and mesh geometry, which can be costly.

name: create_checkpoint
description: Save a persistent .blend checkpoint without overwriting or changing the current document path. Requires Object mode. Stores up to 32 checkpoints in the Blender MCP config directory; use list_checkpoints and delete_checkpoint to manage them. External assets must already be saved on disk; linked files, caches, external side effects, and Python state are not copied. Save failures prevent execution when requested through execute_blender_code.

name: list_checkpoints
description: List saved checkpoint IDs, labels, timestamps, original file paths, file sizes, and object counts. Checkpoints persist across Blender restarts. Restored working copies are separate files and are not listed or deleted by checkpoint management.

name: restore_checkpoint
description: Replace the open Blender document with a working copy of a checkpoint. First saves the current document as a safety checkpoint; requires Object mode and one free checkpoint slot. Clears all execution namespaces. Preserves the current UI, disables file Python auto-execution, and keeps MCP connected. The working copy becomes the current file path; use Save As to save elsewhere. Original files and checkpoint snapshots remain intact. Does not undo external file/network effects, running render jobs, or Python callbacks. Refuses a checkpoint whose saved checksum changed.

name: delete_checkpoint
description: Permanently remove one checkpoint snapshot and its metadata to free storage. Does not change the open scene or remove restored working copies. Refuses to delete a snapshot opened directly as the current file.

name: get_execution_result
description: Retrieve a completed execute_blender_code result that used checkpoint or summarize_changes, including any error, output, checkpoint, and change summary. Omit execution_id for the most recent opted-in result, which can belong to another client: verify namespace and code_sha256. The last eight results are retained in memory until the add-on server restarts. After a timeout, retrieve and inspect before retrying; this command waits behind running Python and does not cancel it. A successful retrieval can contain executed=false from the original failed script.

name: start_render
description: Render one still frame from a snapshot in a separate Blender process. Returns a job_id immediately after the snapshot is written; poll get_render_status, then use get_render_image. Uses the scene's active camera and render settings without changing the open scene. Optional resolution_percentage applies only to this job. Only one job can run at a time. External assets and caches must be saved on disk; Python auto-execution and compositor file-output nodes are disabled in the worker. The latest eight jobs are retained until the add-on server stops. A client timeout does not cancel a job; call get_render_status without job_id to find the latest job before retrying.

scene_name.description: Exact scene name. Omit for the active scene.

frame.description: Frame to render. Omit for the scene's current frame.

resolution_percentage.description: Override the scene's resolution percentage for this job only.

name: get_render_status
description: Get a render job's state, phase, elapsed time, scene, frame, and image availability. States are running, cancelling, completed, cancelled, and failed. A failed job includes error_message. Omit job_id to inspect the latest job, including after an uncertain start_render response. Jobs expire when the add-on server stops or eight newer jobs have started.

job_id.description: Job ID returned by start_render. Omit for the latest job.

name: cancel_render
description: Request cancellation of one render worker without interrupting the open Blender scene. Returns its current status; poll get_render_status until cancelled. Repeated requests are safe. A job that already finished keeps its completed, failed, or cancelled state. Stopping the add-on also stops its render worker.

job_id.description: Exact job ID returned by start_render.

name: get_render_image
description: Return a completed job's camera render as a PNG image with job metadata, returned dimensions, and source dimensions. This is the saved result for that job, independent of later scene changes or renders. The image is scaled down to max_size without changing the saved full-resolution result. Running, failed, cancelled, and expired jobs return an error.

job_id.description: Exact job ID returned by start_render.

max_size.description: Maximum pixel size of the largest returned image dimension.

name: get_sketchfab_status
description:
Check if Sketchfab integration is enabled in Blender.
Returns a message indicating whether Sketchfab features are available.

name: search_sketchfab_models
description:
Search for models on Sketchfab with optional filtering.

Parameters:
- query: Text to search for
- categories: Optional comma-separated list of categories
- count: Maximum number of results to return (default 20)
- downloadable: Whether to include only downloadable models (default True)

Returns a formatted list of matching models.

name: get_sketchfab_model_preview
description:
Get a preview thumbnail of a Sketchfab model by its UID.
Use this to visually confirm a model before downloading.

Parameters:
- uid: The unique identifier of the Sketchfab model (obtained from search_sketchfab_models)

Returns the model's thumbnail as an Image for visual confirmation.

name: download_sketchfab_model
description:
Download and import a Sketchfab model by its UID.
The model will be scaled so its largest dimension equals target_size.

Parameters:
- uid: The unique identifier of the Sketchfab model
- target_size: REQUIRED. The target size in Blender units/meters for the largest dimension.
              You must specify the desired size for the model.
              Examples:
              - Chair: target_size=1.0 (1 meter tall)
              - Table: target_size=0.75 (75cm tall)
              - Car: target_size=4.5 (4.5 meters long)
              - Person: target_size=1.7 (1.7 meters tall)
              - Small object (cup, phone): target_size=0.1 to 0.3

Returns JSON with import details including object names, dimensions, and bounding box.
The model must be downloadable and you must have proper access rights.
